gemini.rationale: The product lines and operational asset base transferred together, so there is no product-process gap (gap_45 = 0). However, the business historically relied on the parent's centralized corporate functions (accounting, IT, HR, etc.) which did not transfer intact, creating a structural gap at the process/organization level (gap_56 = 1). This gap was mitigated at closing via transition services agreements.

grok.rationale: At closing the Power Generation customer-facing products and installed base (T4) crossed together with the segment’s engineering, manufacturing, procurement and erection capabilities (T5) and with the approximately 6,000-person workforce plus incumbent CEO/CFO and named officers (T6), so the slice shows no product-without-process or process-without-organization structural mismatch. Shared corporate functions (accounting, IT, legal, HR, treasury) remained with the parent and were only bridged by transition-services agreements; those functions are not the operational processes that produce the spun products, leaving gap_45 and gap_56 both 0 and gap_mitigated NA.

openai.rationale: The Power Generation product lines crossed with engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and erection capabilities, but the slice states that centralized functions including IT, HR, procurement and supply-chain management, tax, and treasury did not transfer as an intact substrate, establishing a T4-T5 structural gap at closing. That gap was contractually absorbed through transition-services and related separation agreements. No T5-T6 gap is documented because the operating business transferred with approximately 6,000 employees and incumbent management.
